identity.name: Taliban (Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan)
native_names: د افغانستان اسلامي امارت (Də Afghānistān Islāmī Imārat)

land.text: Kandahar City and the country round it, where 'a small Taliban militia first emerged near Kandahar in the spring and summer of 1994' and which it captured in October-November 1994

predecessors.note: Afghanistan was then the Islamic State of Afghanistan (Rabbani) in name only; the pages opened do not say who held Kandahar before the Taliban, so the holders are not named. The movement's years before the Emirate (1994-1996) are drawn from Kandahar alone because the pages are silent on its other gains.

land.text: all the land the Taliban still held when Kabul fell on 13 November 2001 and Kandahar on 7 December 2001, passing to the Northern Alliance / United Front and then the Afghan Interim Administration

successors.note: The Taliban came back to power in August 2021; that return belongs to the afghanistan dossier. Cliopatria's Taliban row runs to 2005; the pages opened show no Taliban-held territory after December 2001.

capitals.name: Kandahar
capitals.note: Taliban page infobox: headquarters Kandahar (1994-2001; 2021-present). Mullah Omar stayed in Kandahar after 1996; it is the movement's base, not the Emirate's listed capital.

rulers.name: Mullah Omar
rulers.title: supreme leader (Amir al-Mu'minin from 1996)
rulers.note: Taliban page infobox: supreme leader Mullah Omar (1994-2013); the Emirate page names Mullah Omar and Mohammad Rabbani (1996-2001) as its leaders, Abdul Kabir acting leader in 2001, and dates Omar's proclamation as leader to 4 April 1996 in Kandahar.

correction.text: Kandahar City, 'captured' by the Taliban marching from Maiwand in October-November 1994

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Taliban row starts in 1996. The page dates only the capture of Kandahar (October-November 1994); it is silent on the movement's gains of 1995, so this outline is a floor, not the real extent, and a gap-filler should open the 1995 Herat and Helmand campaigns.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1996 outline less Bamyan province (the Taliban page dates the taking of 'the town of Bamian' to 1999) and less its 17 grid cells in Pakistan; the shape holds 1996-1997 only, since 1998 adds the north

keyframe_review.note: 413,000 km2 on the grid (450,887 in shapes.csv) against the infobox 587,580 km2 (ratio 0.77 by the Cliopatria figure): inside a factor of two. The shape reaches Kabul, Nangarhar, Herat and the south but not Balkh or Kunduz, so it fits the position after 27 September 1996 and is too large for January-September 1996 (Kabul fell only then). The gazetteer puts the whole of Bamyan inside; that province was Hazarajat, which the pages show taken later (1998-1999).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 2000 outline less the Taloqan district of Takhar (taken 5 September 2000), less Bamyan (taken 1999) and less its Pakistani cells: the north to the Amu Darya from Mazar-i-Sharif, the extent of 'By 1998, the Taliban controlled 90% of Afghanistan'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria keeps the 1996 outline to 1999 although the page says 'By 1998, the Taliban controlled 90% of Afghanistan'; the 1996 outline is only 63% of the country. The 2000 outline (560,314 km2, 95% of the infobox 587,580) is the nearest Cliopatria figure to that 90%, so it is used for 1998 with the two later gains taken out. The pages name Mazar-i-Sharif (8 August 1998) but no other northern town, so the provinces between Mazar and Kunduz are Cliopatria's reading (confidence 2 in the ledger).

correction.text: the 1998 outline plus Bamyan, 'In 1999, the town of Bamian was taken'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Bamiyan is the one 1999 gain the pages date. The Northern Alliance page puts the defeat of the Hezb-e Wahdat in 1998, the Taliban page the taking of Bamian in 1999; 1999 is used.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 2000 outline less its Pakistani cells; the shape holds 2000-2001 only, ending when Kandahar fell on 7 December 2001

keyframe_review.note: 560,314 km2 against the infobox 587,580 km2 (ratio 0.95): consistent; the page says the Taliban held about 90% at the end of 2000, the Northern Alliance about 10% (65,284 km2) mainly in Badakhshan, which the shape leaves out. Cliopatria runs the shape to 2005, but 'The Islamic Emirate ceased to exist on 7 December 2001' and the Taliban page shows an insurgency from 2002, not a state with territory; 2002-2005 should be drawn as Afghanistan.

region.text: Kandahar City and its province: 'A small Taliban militia first emerged near Kandahar in the spring and summer of 1994'; the Taliban marched from Maiwand in October-November 1994 to capture Kandahar City

ledger.note: 1994: Mullah Omar's Taliban emerge near Kandahar and take the city. The page gives 'spring and summer of 1994' for the militia and October-November 1994 for Kandahar; no day; the Emirate itself was proclaimed in 1996. The holders of Kandahar before the capture are not named on the page.

region.text: the south, west and east between Kandahar, Herat and Jalalabad that Cliopatria's 1996 outline holds; the pages opened give no dates for them

ledger.note: 1996: by the proclamation of the Emirate the Taliban hold the south and west as well as Kandahar. Bridging entry: the page is silent on the 1995 campaigns and on the east, so this is inferred from the shape Cliopatria draws from 1996, not read from a page.

27 September 1996: the Taliban take Kabul. Infobox 'Capture of Kabul: 27 September 1996'; the Northern Alliance page adds that 'The Taliban seized Kabul on September 27, 1996' after Massoud ordered a retreat. The page names the city, the province is the reading.
September 1996: Kabul becomes the capital of the Emirate (infobox 'Capital Kabul'); Mullah Omar remained at Kandahar, the movement's base.

27 September 1996: the Taliban movement becomes the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan. 'The Taliban seized Kabul on September 27, 1996, and established the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.' The Emirate page dates Mullah Omar's proclamation as leader to 4 April 1996 in Kandahar. The Emirate page's infobox has a later step, 'Name changed to "Emirate": 29 October 1997' (reviewer ia-03-h); the rename is kept at September 1996, the Northern Alliance page's date.

region.text: the north-east the Northern Alliance held: Badakhshan, Takhar, Kapisa and the Panjshir ('Massoud controlled Panjshir'); the Alliance's base moved to Badakhshan

ledger.note: September 1996: the Northern Alliance forms against the Taliban and the front moves north and east of Kabul. The page lists Badakhshan, Kapisa, Takhar, parts of Parwan, Kunar, Nuristan, Laghman, Samangan, Kunduz, Ghor and Bamyan among the provinces the Alliance held; the zone here is its enduring core, not every province on the list.

region.text: the provinces between Mazar-i-Sharif and Kunduz that Cliopatria adds in 2000, held by 1998: 'By 1998, the Taliban controlled 90% of Afghanistan'

ledger.note: 1998: the Taliban reach 90% of Afghanistan. 'By 1998, the Taliban controlled 90% of Afghanistan under their interpretation of Sharia.' The page names no northern town but Mazar-i-Sharif; the year is the page's, the provinces are the reading of Cliopatria's 2000 outline.

region.text: Mazar-i-Sharif: 'On 8 August 1998, the Taliban launched an attack on Mazar-i-Sharif'

ledger.note: 8 August 1998: the Taliban attack Mazar-i-Sharif and break Dostum's northern base. 'On 8 August 1998, the Taliban launched an attack on Mazar-i-Sharif', 'Of the 1500 defenders only 100 survived'; the Northern Alliance page says Dostum's forces 'were defeated by the Taliban and their allies in 1998' and that the city had been 'overrun in 1997'. The capture itself is not dated on the pages opened.

region.text: the town of Bamian and, by the reading here, its province

ledger.note: 1999: the Taliban take Bamiyan. 'In 1999, the town of Bamian was taken, and hundreds of men, women and children were executed.' The Northern Alliance page puts the defeat of the Hezb-e Wahdat in 1998. The Emirate page puts it earlier: 'After Battles of Mazar-i-Sharif (1997-98), the Bamyan valley came into Taliban control' (reviewer ia-03-h).

5 September 2000: the Taliban take Taloqan. The city 'was the group's headquarters until September 5, 2000, when the city was taken by the Taliban', which 'led to its base moving to Badakhshan Province'.

13 November 2001: Kabul falls to the Northern Alliance, five weeks after the US-led invasion began on 7 October 2001. Infobox 'Fall of Kabul: 13 November 2001'. The Northern Alliance page says that 'Between November and December 2001, the United Front gained control of most major Afghan cities'; the pages date no other city.

region.text: the rest of the Emirate's land, with Kandahar its last city: 'Fall of Kandahar: 7 December 2001'

ledger.note: 7 December 2001: Kandahar falls and the Taliban lose the last of their land. Infobox 'Fall of Kandahar: 7 December 2001'; 'The Islamic Emirate ceased to exist on 7 December 2001.' The northern cities fell between the two dates (Northern Alliance page) but are not individually dated.

region.text: the north-east front, ended by the fall of the regime

ledger.note: December 2001: the Taliban-Alliance front ends with the fall of the Emirate; the Northern Alliance page says the Alliance 'controlled only about 5% of the country' by 2001 before the collapse.

region.text: all that remained of the Emirate

ledger.note: 7 December 2001: the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan falls. 'The Islamic Emirate ceased to exist on 7 December 2001'; its land passes to the Northern Alliance / United Front and then the Afghan Interim Administration.

wars.name: Taliban offensives against the Northern Alliance (Afghan civil war, 1996-2001)

zones.text: the north-east the Alliance kept: Badakhshan, Takhar and the Panjshir

wars.outcome: The Taliban took Kabul (27 September 1996), Mazar-i-Sharif (1998), Bamiyan (1999) and the Alliance headquarters Taloqan (5 September 2000) and held about 90% of the country; the Alliance, pushed to Badakhshan and the Panjshir, outlasted them and took Kabul on 13 November 2001.
wars.note: The Alliance held roughly 30% of the population from September 1996 to November 2001 but only about 5% of the territory by 2001 (page).

wars.name: Battles of Mazar-i-Sharif (1997-1998)
wars.outcome: The city 'was overrun in 1997' and Dostum's forces 'were defeated by the Taliban and their allies in 1998'; the Taliban page dates their attack to 8 August 1998.
wars.note: The pages opened do not say how the city changed hands in 1997 (the Taliban held it only briefly); only the 1998 outcome is used in the ledger.

wars.name: War in Afghanistan (2001-2021): the US-led invasion of 2001
wars.outcome: Invasion begins 7 October 2001; Kabul falls 13 November and Kandahar 7 December, ending the Islamic Emirate.
wars.note: Territorially the Taliban lose everything to the Northern Alliance and its allies; no zone is contested because the front collapses within two months.

certainty.note: Control was by front lines and cities held, not surveyed frontiers; the outer frontier with Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Pakistan along the Amu Darya and the Durand Line is a treaty line, but the pages opened say nothing of it, so the whole life is soft.

sources.title: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (1996-2001)
sources.note: Identity, capital, area 587,580 km2, 90% control by 1998, Kabul 27 September 1996, the 2001 invasion and fall; opened with the en dash in the title.

sources.title: Taliban
sources.note: Origins in Kandahar 1994, headquarters, Mullah Omar, Mazar attack 8 August 1998, Bamiyan 1999, the post-2001 insurgency. No dates for Herat, Jalalabad or Taloqan.

sources.title: Northern Alliance
sources.note: Kabul 27 September 1996, Mazar 1997-1998, Taloqan 5 September 2000, the Alliance's territory, December 2001; opened twice (second time for the Taloqan sentence).

notes: Taliban, Cliopatria row 1996-2005 (2 shapes), re-dated 1994-2001: the Taliban movement emerges near Kandahar in 1994, proclaims the Emirate in 1996 and falls on 7 December 2001. Cliopatria's second shape runs to 2005; the pages show no Taliban territory after 2001, so 2002-2005 is Afghanistan (adjust verdict with years). Both Cliopatria shapes contain 17 grid cells in Pakistan, removed in the corrections. The 1996 outline contains all of Bamyan, which the pages show taken in 1998-1999. Gaps for a gap-filler: the 1995 Taliban campaigns (Helmand, Herat) and the siege of Kabul before September 1996, Jalalabad (Sept 1996), the date and place of every northern town taken in 1998 and 2000 (Kunduz, Sar-e Pol, Faryab, Samangan, Baghlan), the Hazarajat. Page budget (1-2) exceeded by one page (Northern Alliance) because the Taloqan and Mazar dates were on no other page; the Afghanistan dossier (ia-03) holds the matching losses with other pages. The Islamic State of Afghanistan (Rabbani, 1992-1996) and the Northern Alliance are not separate dossiers: they sit in afghanistan. Gazetteer names used: all in Natural Earth and the places list (Taloqan, Kandahar, Kabul, Bamyan, Balkh, Takhar, Kapisa, Parwan, Badakhshan).
